title: bhf.collector-event.v1
description: One line of the platform-neutral runtime-event collector stream (JSONL). A collector observes the process, filesystem, and module-load effects a target performs while a testcase runs — including effects on a clean exit — so an out-of-repo provider (native Windows ETW, an external sidecar) can target this wire format and feed the bhf oracle layer. `phase` is a closed enum; `kind` is left open so a newer provider can emit a family an older host preserves as unknown rather than dropping.

phase.description: Testcase lifecycle marker: `begin`/`end` bracket the testcase, `event` is everything observed in between.

kind.description: Normalized event family. Known values: process_create, shell_execute, file_create, file_open, file_write, file_rename, file_delete, module_load, network, registry. Other strings are preserved (forward compatibility), not rejected.

process.description: Identity of the acting process. `ancestor` is the testcase root pid attribution keys on; `parent` is the immediate parent; `user`/`token`/`session` capture the security principal.

fidelity.description: Collection-fidelity metadata. Any of these signals must block a 'clean' assurance so a degraded observation never masquerades as 'the target did nothing dangerous'.
